description: PRD-216 — CI/CD Security Gates. The live `.github/workflows/ci.yml` already gates on typecheck + `pnpm lint` + `pnpm build` (lint IS enforced; the first review's 'lint disabled' claim was wrong). The REAL gaps: (1) no test step at all, (2) no Dependabot, (3) no CodeQL, (4) no secret scanning, (5) no SBOM, (6) `eslint.ignoreDuringBuilds:true` suppresses lint in `next build` only, (7) the cross-PRD security grep gates aren't run per-PR so fixed findings can silently regress. This PRD adds those gates on top of the existing typecheck+lint+build baseline. App lives in nextjs_space/ (pnpm 9, Node 20, Next 14.2.35). CI runs with working-directory: nextjs_space. GROUNDED REALITY verified on this branch (off main): PRD-200's grep gates already exist as robust string-aware node scripts at nextjs_space/scripts/ci/{check-css-sanitized,check-no-error-message-leaks,strip-strings}.mjs and PASS, but are NOT wired into ci.yml (only into package.json `check:security`). PRD-202's removal is NOT merged — lib/tenant.ts still has 12 setTenantContext( + 3 enterWith( calls. PRD-215 redaction is NOT merged — ~42 console/logger lines still reference PII field names. PRD-207's vitest harness is NOT merged — there is no `test`/`test:cov` script and no vitest config. CONSEQUENCE: gates whose source-PRD cleanup has not landed (test gate→PRD-207, PRD-202 gate, PRD-215 gate, docs-lint→PRD-214) are authored now but wired REPORT-ONLY / non-blocking (continue-on-error) so they do not red the build on pre-existing debt; each carries a documented condition to flip to blocking once its source PRD merges. PRD-200 gates wire as BLOCKING immediately (they pass). Source PRD: docs/PRDS/REMEDIATION/PRD-216-ci-cd-security-gates.md. Global rules: never commit/echo a real secret VALUE (only key NAMES); the ci.yml stub keys (ENCRYPTION_KEY=0000…0000, pk_test_stub, sk_test_stub) are throwaway and must be allow-listed in the secret scanner; never hardcode template-specific values; minimal in-scope diffs only.

userStories.title: PRD-202 grep gate script — no enterWith()/setTenantContext()
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I want a CI-runnable script that flags any `enterWith(` or `setTenantContext(` so PRD-202's tenant-context fix cannot silently regress once it lands.
acceptanceCriteria: Create nextjs_space/scripts/ci/check-no-tenant-context-escapes.mjs following the existing string-aware pattern (reuse blankNonCode/offsetToLineCol from ./strip-strings.mjs so matches inside string literals/comments do not count)

It scans nextjs_space app/, lib/, components/, middleware.ts (recursively, .ts/.tsx/.js/.mjs), excluding node_modules, .next, dist, and the scripts/ci/ directory itself (so the gate's own regex literal cannot self-trip)

It exits non-zero and prints each hit as `path:line:col → enterWith(/setTenantContext( — PRD-202: set tenant context only via runWithTenantContext()/withTenantContext()` (failure message names file:line AND owning PRD per AC-7a)
Add package.json script `check:no-tenant-escapes`: `node scripts/ci/check-no-tenant-context-escapes.mjs`

Sanity: `node --check scripts/ci/check-no-tenant-context-escapes.mjs` passes; running the script on this tree reports the ~15 KNOWN pre-existing occurrences in lib/tenant.ts (proving detection works) — these are PRD-202's to remove, NOT this story's; do NOT edit lib/tenant.ts
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: DO NOT modify lib/tenant.ts — removing those calls is PRD-202's scope, explicitly out-of-scope here (PRD-216 §5). This story only WRITES the detector. Because the real occurrences still exist, the gate will be wired REPORT-ONLY in US-003 until PRD-202 merges. Read nextjs_space/scripts/ci/strip-strings.mjs and check-no-error-message-leaks.mjs first and mirror their structure exactly. Watch the self-match trap: the regex source contains the literal token, so exclude scripts/ci/ from the scan AND/OR build the pattern so the checker file is skipped.

userStories.title: PRD-215 grep gate script — no PII field names in raw logs
userStories.description: As security, I want a CI-runnable script that flags PII field names (email, firstName, phone, address, drGreenResponse, etc.) interpolated into raw console.*/logger.* calls, so PRD-215's redaction cannot silently regress once it lands.
acceptanceCriteria: Create nextjs_space/scripts/ci/check-no-pii-in-logs.mjs (string-aware via strip-strings.mjs) that finds console.(log|error|warn|info|debug)(…) and logger.<level>(…) call sites whose argument span references a banned PII identifier (email, body.email, clerkUser.email, firstName, phone, address, drGreenResponse) — either as an interpolated ${…} expression or as a bare argument identifier
It exits non-zero and prints each hit as `path:line:col → <token> in console/logger call — PRD-215/213: redact PII before logging (use lib/redact.ts)` (file:line + owning PRD per AC-7a)
Add package.json script `check:no-pii-logs`: `node scripts/ci/check-no-pii-in-logs.mjs`

Sanity: `node --check` passes; running on this tree reports the ~42 KNOWN pre-existing hits (e.g. app/tenant-admin/layout.tsx, app/actions/kyc-check.ts) — these are PRD-215's to fix, NOT this story's; do NOT edit those call sites
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Heuristic gate — bias toward the exact PII identifiers named in PRD-216 AC-7 to keep false-positives low; it is wired REPORT-ONLY in US-003 until PRD-215 redaction merges, so over-matching is non-fatal but avoid it. DO NOT modify any logging call sites — that is PRD-215/213 scope, out-of-scope here. Mirror the existing .mjs gate structure. Pure detector only.

userStories.title: Unified grep-gate runner + wire into ci.yml (PRD-200 blocking; 202/215 report-only)
userStories.description: As a developer, when I open a PR the security grep gates run automatically: PRD-200 gates fail the build, PRD-202/215 gates report as non-blocking warnings until their source PRDs land.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a thin repo-root runner scripts/ci/grep-gates.sh that runs the BLOCKING set (PRD-200: `pnpm --dir nextjs_space check:security`) and exits non-zero on any failure; usable locally and in CI
Add package.json `check:grep-gates:report` that runs the report-only set (check:no-tenant-escapes + check:no-pii-logs) and always exits 0 (e.g. `|| true` per gate) while still printing findings
Edit .github/workflows/ci.yml: add a BLOCKING step `Security grep gates (PRD-200)` after Lint running `pnpm check:security` (working-directory nextjs_space, already the job default)

Add a NON-BLOCKING step `Regression grep gates (PRD-202/215 — report-only)` with `continue-on-error: true` running `pnpm check:grep-gates:report`, with an inline comment: flip to blocking once PRD-202 (enterWith/setTenantContext removal) and PRD-215 (log redaction) merge
ci.yml remains valid GitHub Actions YAML (parses cleanly) and the existing typecheck/lint/build steps are unchanged
`bash scripts/ci/grep-gates.sh` exits 0 on this tree (PRD-200 gates pass)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-001 + US-002. The existing PRD-200 gates pass, so wiring `check:security` blocking is safe NOW. The PRD-202/215 gates would fail on pre-existing debt (15 + 42 hits), so they MUST be non-blocking (continue-on-error) — this mirrors the PRD's own treatment of the test gate (AC-1) and docs-lint (AC-7b). The PRD names `scripts/ci/grep-gates.sh` (repo root); satisfy that path but reuse the robust nextjs_space/scripts/ci/*.mjs gates rather than re-implementing in bash. Read the current ci.yml (job 'Typecheck · Lint · Build', working-directory nextjs_space) before editing; keep the diff additive.

userStories.title: Advisory docs-lint (PRD-214) — non-blocking ci.yml step
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a non-blocking CI warning if banned docs patterns (next-auth, abacus, banned sales claims) are reintroduced, per PRD-214.
acceptanceCriteria: Create nextjs_space/scripts/ci/check-docs-lint.mjs (or scripts/ci/docs-lint.mjs at repo root) that scans docs/ and README files for the PRD-214 banned patterns: `next-auth`, `abacus` (case-insensitive), and the banned sales-claim phrases referenced by PRD-214

It prints findings as `path:line → <pattern> — PRD-214 advisory` but is ADVISORY: the script itself may exit non-zero, but the CI step that runs it uses continue-on-error: true so it never fails the build
Add package.json script `check:docs-lint` and a NON-BLOCKING ci.yml step `Docs lint (PRD-214 — advisory)` with continue-on-error: true

Read PRD-214 (docs/PRDS/REMEDIATION/PRD-214*.md) for the exact banned phrases; if PRD-214 is absent, use the patterns named in PRD-216 AC-7b (next-auth, abacus, banned sales claims) and note the assumption in progress.txt
ci.yml remains valid YAML; node --check passes on the new script
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Always non-blocking (AC-7b). Keep the pattern list small and exact. This is a warning surface, not a gate. If PRD-214's md is not present on this branch, fall back to the AC-7b patterns and record the fallback in the journal.

userStories.title: Dependabot config (.github/dependabot.yml)
userStories.description: As security, I want Dependabot opening grouped weekly dependency-update PRs and flagging new CVEs for the pnpm app and the GitHub Actions workflows.
acceptanceCriteria: Create .github/dependabot.yml (version: 2) with two update entries

Entry 1: package-ecosystem: npm, directory: /nextjs_space (pnpm is read via package-ecosystem npm), schedule weekly, grouped minor+patch updates, open-pull-requests-limit set (e.g. 5) so it does not flood, labels added
Entry 2: package-ecosystem: github-actions, directory: /, schedule weekly, grouped
Security updates are enabled (default-on for Dependabot; do not disable). Add a brief comment documenting the grouping + limit rationale
File is valid YAML and conforms to Dependabot v2 schema (keys: version, updates[].package-ecosystem/directory/schedule/groups/open-pull-requests-limit)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: directory must point at /nextjs_space because pnpm-lock.yaml + package.json live there, not repo root. Use package-ecosystem: npm (Dependabot reads pnpm-lock.yaml under the npm ecosystem). Pure config file; no app code. Verify against the Dependabot v2 schema.

userStories.title: CodeQL workflow (.github/workflows/codeql.yml)
userStories.description: As security, I want CodeQL static analysis on every PR to main plus a weekly schedule, using the security-and-quality query suite.
acceptanceCriteria: Create .github/workflows/codeql.yml: triggers on pull_request to main, push to main, and a weekly schedule (cron)
Uses github/codeql-action init+analyze with languages: javascript-typescript and queries: security-and-quality
Has the required permissions block (security-events: write, actions: read, contents: read)

Per OQ-4: a comment documents the rollout — warn/baseline on first run, then HIGH/CRITICAL introduced by a PR should block (no autofail config needed in YAML; this is a repo branch-protection decision, documented in the workflow comment)
File is valid GitHub Actions YAML; uses currently-pinned action major versions (codeql-action v3, checkout v4)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Standard CodeQL workflow. No build-mode customisation needed for JS/TS (none/auto). Do not add matrix languages we do not use. The hard-block-vs-triage decision (OQ-4) is enforced via GitHub branch protection by Gerard, not in YAML — just document it in a comment.

userStories.title: Secret-scan workflow (gitleaks) + .gitleaks.toml allow-list
userStories.description: As security, I want gitleaks scanning every PR diff (and full history on schedule) and failing the PR on a detected secret, with the known CI stub keys allow-listed.
acceptanceCriteria: Create .github/workflows/secret-scan.yml running gitleaks (gitleaks/gitleaks-action or the gitleaks CLI) on pull_request + push, and a scheduled full-history scan; a detected secret fails the PR

Create .gitleaks.toml at repo root extending the default config with an allowlist covering the ci.yml stub VALUES (the 64-hex ENCRYPTION_KEY `0000…0000`, `pk_test_stub`, `sk_test_stub`, `postgresql://stub:stub@localhost:5432/stub`, NEXTAUTH_SECRET `stub`) and paths like .env.example/.env.test
The allowlist is by regex/stopword for those exact stub values and/or by path for .github/workflows/ci.yml — so the stubs do NOT trip the scanner

Both files are valid (YAML + TOML parse). If the gitleaks CLI happens to be installed locally, `gitleaks detect --no-git -c .gitleaks.toml` over the repo does NOT flag the ci.yml stubs; if not installed, validate config syntax only and note it
NEVER add a real secret value anywhere in these files — only the already-public throwaway stubs
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Per OQ-3 the chosen scanner is gitleaks. The allow-list MUST cover exactly the stub keys already committed in .github/workflows/ci.yml (read that file for the exact values) so CI does not self-flag. Do not weaken detection beyond those stubs. gitleaks is likely NOT installed on this box — if so, just validate TOML/YAML syntax and record that the live run is verified post-merge on GitHub.

userStories.title: SBOM generation workflow (CycloneDX JSON) + artifact upload

Use a generator that supports pnpm — prefer @cyclonedx/cdxgen or anchore/syft (sbom-action); if using @cyclonedx/cyclonedx-npm note its pnpm caveats. Output format: CycloneDX JSON (e.g. sbom.cdx.json)
Triggers on push to main + a manual workflow_dispatch (and optionally attaches to releases)

userStories.title: Flip eslint.ignoreDuringBuilds to false in next.config.js
userStories.description: As a developer, I want `next build` to also enforce lint (defence-in-depth) since CI already runs pnpm lint separately.
acceptanceCriteria: Set nextjs_space/next.config.js eslint.ignoreDuringBuilds to false (currently true at :12). Leave typescript.ignoreBuildErrors as false (already correct at :15) — do not touch it

Run `cd nextjs_space && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (if needed) then `pnpm build` with the same stub env ci.yml uses (DATABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, CLERK_SECRET_KEY, NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_DOMAIN, NEXTAUTH_SECRET, ENCRYPTION_KEY)

If the build now surfaces lint errors: fix them if small/obvious; if it is a large backlog, REVERT the flag (keep ignoreDuringBuilds:true), record the finding under PRD-216 §13 OQ-2 in the PRD doc + progress.txt, and mark this story BLOCKED (emit RALPH_BLOCKED) rather than half-shipping
If the build passes with the flag false: keep it. `pnpm lint` still passes; `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` still passes
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: CI lint (pnpm lint) already passes on main, and next build uses the same ESLint config, so the delta SHOULD be near-zero — but verify by actually running the build, do not assume. This is the one story with a conditional BLOCK: if flipping surfaces a real lint backlog that blocks the build and it is not a quick fix, revert + document OQ-2 + RALPH_BLOCKED. Build needs the stub env vars; export them inline for the build command only (throwaway values, never real secrets).

userStories.title: Non-blocking test-gate job in ci.yml (wires PRD-207 when it lands)

Because PRD-207 has not merged (no `test`/`test:cov` script, no vitest config yet), the step is NON-BLOCKING: guard it so a missing script does not fail the build — e.g. `continue-on-error: true` AND/OR a guard like `pnpm run | grep -q test:cov && pnpm test:cov || echo 'PRD-207 suites not present yet — skipping'`

Per OQ-1: a comment notes Playwright runs a tagged critical-path subset on PR and the full suite on main (the actual Playwright wiring is PRD-207's; this job just reserves/structures the gate)
ci.yml is valid YAML; existing steps unchanged
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Soft-depends on PRD-207, which is NOT merged — that's why this is non-blocking now (the PRD explicitly allows 'starts as a non-blocking job that becomes blocking when the suites land'). Do NOT invent a vitest config or test script here — that's PRD-207's scope. Only author the CI job + guard + the flip-to-blocking note. This is the LAST story: when it's done (and all others done/blocked), emit RALPH_COMPLETE.
